On Linux/macOS with `bubblewrap`/`seatbelt`, `ready` is derived from `sandboxUsable` (`services/runner/src/readiness.ts:78-79`), so disagreement (a) cannot arise there — though the sandboxed branch is the one that already derives its verdict from a probe, which is what section 2 item 4 asks the `none` branch to do.
- The managed starter environment must be unprovisionable at check time (here `micromamba create` failing on a corrupt package cache), so `shellCapability()` answers `available: false` with a reason (`services/runner/src/environment-store.ts:445-446` / `:463-464`). Any Shell-probe failure should do: the probe is a file/executability check plus the environment store's own creation state, and it runs no user code.
- The Agent must ask. Because `runnerReadiness.check` drops the argument (`workspace-bindings.ts:416`), `check_runner` answers the Python question whatever the Agent meant; the disagreement surfaces as soon as the Agent then takes the Shell route.
- Not required: wall-clock timeouts, model behaviour, sandbox permissions, remote Runners, the specific package-cache error. An older Runner that reports no `shell` field at all shows no contradiction — by design (`:191-192`), which is also why a fix must keep treating an absent field as unknown rather than as unavailable.
- Deterministic reproduction: run the Runner on Windows against a data directory whose starter-env revision cannot be created (or otherwise force `shellCapability()` to answer `available: false`); from one Agent, call `check_runner` and then any Shell tool, and compare `ready`/`reason` in the two results against the `capability` blocks, which will match except for `checkedAt`. A unit-level version needs a test that goes through the workspace tool registry rather than calling `checkRunner` directly, because the binding's default is the thing under test.

## 6. Difference from existing Issues and PRs

The PI ruling required checking the *actual* repair scope of #1095 and #1081 against their own patches before deciding whether E-5A is a duplicate. Both checks came out negative, so the draft stands independently.

- **PR #1095** `fix(workspace): preserve actionable shell diagnostics in model results` — merged `2026-11-11T11:40:15Z`, squash commit `a773942a46a5…`, head `c488e0b3…`, base `f61cb5e4…`. Five files: `packages/workspace/src/shell-diagnostic-view.test.ts` (new, +53), `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` (+5/-0), `scripts/stack-platform.test.mjs` (+16/-3), `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.test.ts` (+2/-0), `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` (+1/-1). Its two code changes are (i) `shellExecutionModelView` gains a `diagnostic` object (`code`/`command`/`instruction`) so a *failed Shell execution result* keeps its interpretation, and (ii) one prose line at `workspace-bindings.ts:237` inside the `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` instruction. It does **not** touch `services/runner/src/readiness.ts`, `environment-store.ts`, `server.ts`, `packages/schema/src/environment.ts`, the `checkRunner` signature, or the `runnerReadiness.check` binding. Confirmed at blob level: main `6664fc9b1fb7` and the copy our instance runs `8bcb6326e93f` differ at line `:237` only. **In short: #1095 improved what a refused Shell call explains after the refusal; it did not change what `check_runner` claims before it.** Not a duplicate.
- **Issue #1081** `[Bug]: Readiness reports a dead provider integration as ready, because catalog.ts never probes it` — **open**, and there is no PR #1081. Same *class* as ours (a readiness verdict derived without consulting a probe), different subsystem: the plugin/provider catalog (`services/api/src/plugins/catalog.ts`), sharing no code path with Runner execution readiness. Its own framing is the expectation we rely on ("the product kept reporting ready while the download path was dead"; readiness "only reads configuration, never a probe result"). Our case is one step further along the same shape: the Runner **does** probe, **does** report `available: false`, and the headline verdict still ignores it. A fix there would not fix this, and closing #1081 would not make our payload consistent. Not a duplicate.
- **PR #716** `fix(runner): provide a managed Windows shell toolchain` — merged `2026-11-07T10:00:12Z`, head `deafeb0a…`, 24 files including `readiness.ts` (+16/-5), `environment-store.ts` (+70/-2), `workspace-bindings.ts` (+39/-12), `packages/schema/src/environment.ts` (+13/-0). This is the change that introduced the `shell` sub-capability, the `sandbox === "none"` → `ready: true` branch, and the `requiresShell` parameter — and, in the same hunk, put the failure transcript and the word `"ready"` into one object (`detail: shell?.unavailableReason ?? "unsandboxed direct execution"` added next to an unchanged `ready: true, reason: "ready"`). It threaded `requiresShell` through the execution and wait paths but not through the tool-facing `check` binding. We are not disputing its design intent (Python must not be blocked by a Shell gap); this is the residual on the diagnostic surface it left open, and its own comment at `:35-37` is the reason we expect the fix to be a route-scoped answer rather than a new block.
- **Issue #916** (Windows managed Shell missing base Unix utilities; diagnosable environment capability) — closed by #716. It asked that the capability be *reported*; `shell` now is, and the suggestions do name the repair. What it did not get is a headline verdict that reflects the reported answer.
- **Issue #461 / PR #463** `fix(runner): report egress socket path readiness` — both the bug shape and the fix shape we propose, already applied once to a sibling sub-capability: #461's title is "…so every run_shell fails **while the Runner reports ready**", and #463 made `sandboxNetworkCapability` probe its own dependency and return `{ available: false, modes: ["none"], unavailableReason: … }` so `/health` never "advertises a mode whose first command would fail". Different probe, different code, closed and verified here — cited as precedent, not as a duplicate.
- **Issue #265** (decouple sandbox readiness from installation and workbench startup; offer choices when execution is blocked) — the philosophy the `suggestions` and `wait_for_runner` card implement. Our ask stays inside it: the card is right; the headline verdict should not contradict it, and the cancel branch should not return a check-free answer into an Agent that asked for a recheck.
- **Issue #29** (dependency preflight failures should say how to fix them, not just what is missing) — satisfied: `suggestions[0]` names the repair. That is also why `reason: "ready"` next to it reads as a bug rather than as missing information.
- Repo search found no Issue or PR mentioning `shell.available` at all; `check_runner` appears only in #461, #916 and the 0.3.0-rc1 RFC #343.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

1. No model-visible `check_runner` payload may carry `reason: "ready"` (or a `ready: true` presented as an execution green light) while the same payload carries `capability.shell.available: false`, unless the payload names the route the verdict applies to. Consistency must be structural, not something a consumer recovers by parsing a nested field.
2. The two surfaces must agree about the same Runner state within a short window: a `check_runner` answer and the `runner` block of the next Shell refusal should not disagree in the headline. A test should assert that pair, since the whole defect is invisible from either object alone.
3. `capability.ready` / `capability.reason` on the `sandbox === "none"` branch must be derived from the probe the way `:78-79` derives them on the sandboxed branch, not fixed as literals — so a consumer reading `capability` is not reading a constant.
4. Whichever shape from section 2 is chosen, it must be documented where a caller reads it: the `check_runner` tool description and the `RunnerExecutionCapability` doc comment. If `ready` keeps the Python-channel meaning, the description must say that it ignores `shell.available`.
5. A test drives the **tool** path, not `checkRunner` directly: sandbox `"none"`, a `shellProbe` returning `available: false`, then `check_runner` executed through the workspace tool registry, asserting the model-visible `ready`/`reason`. Today only tests that re-implement the binding's default can pass.
6. The Runner must say so at startup. `services/runner/src/server.ts:1189` cannot fire on this branch, so a warning (or equivalent operator-visible signal) on `capability.shell?.available === false` at startup is required; the entire 10-hour capture produced no startup complaint.
7. `wait_for_runner`'s cancel/expired branch should either carry the fresh check it just performed or not tell the caller to "use check_runner" to recheck a blocker it cannot report (`:444-445` vs `:206`).
8. Duplication in the diagnostic payload should be bounded (one transcript, referenced rather than repeated in `capability.detail`, `capability.shell.unavailableReason` and `suggestions[0]`), so the verdict is not buried in a 14 KB result. Acceptance is a size bound, not a wording change.
9. Behaviour that must NOT regress: Shell gaps never block Python execution; an absent `shell` field stays "unknown", not "unavailable" (`:191-192`); the `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` repair instruction and the `wait_for_runner` card stay as #1095 and #265 delivered them.

## 8. Version this draft measured

- SD main when this draft was finalised: `bec6399dc18afe8885af94080988d5e28538f4b8` (2026-11-11T12:27:01Z). The one commit between it and the anchor base `a773942a46a59239e5fe425fb800343086b48f43` touches `apps/desktop/` only, and the blob ids listed below are unchanged at both, so no line number in this draft shifts.
- Line numbers were anchored at `a773942a46a59239e5fe425fb800343086b48f43` (PR #1095 squash, merged `2026-11-11T11:40:15Z`). The preceding main tip measured this round was `1d54705431ee…`; every line number above was re-read at `a773942a46a5…` from the GitHub contents API, and only the `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` citations shift (by 5 lines).
- Local upstream clone at the time of comparison: `d6f3b20ca2440a3dfb2eb3c922d54d22be6cdb46` (33 commits behind main); the downstream fork our instance runs is `30178fda7…`. Blob identity (main / local upstream / fork): `services/runner/src/readiness.ts` `47c678febd07` / same / same; `services/runner/src/environment-store.ts` `268e0049660b` / same / same; `services/runner/src/executor.ts` `d0a12151eeb8` / same / same; `services/runner/src/server.ts` `053bc98da55c` / same / same; `packages/schema/src/environment.ts` `424a1559fad3` / same / same; `services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts` `6664fc9b1fb7` / `8bcb6326e93f` / `8bcb6326e93f` (differ at line 237 only); `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `11ddfadfc244` / `b85342f13264` / `b85342f13264`.
- Consequence: the capture was produced by code one prose line behind main in one file and byte-identical to main in every file that derives the verdict or runs the probe. The shape reported here is main's shape, and section 6 shows it is not closed by #1095.

## Limitations of this report

- All runtime evidence comes from one Windows host on the `sandbox: "none"` direct-execution path. We have not measured `bubblewrap`/`seatbelt` startup behaviour for this shape, and we do not claim the disagreement occurs there.
- The corpus contains no healthy-host control: every occurrence we have reports `shell.available: false`, so we cannot show from evidence what the same code prints when the Shell probe succeeds. The code says `ready: true` either way, and that is exactly what makes the field uninformative — but the "misleading on a healthy host" case is inferred from source, not observed.
- Occurrence counts (194) are a census of objects in persisted streams, not a count of tool calls (3 `check_runner`, 1 `wait_for_runner`). They are reported side by side because the ratio between them is itself a property of the capture, and because a first pass that read only one unit produced a materially wrong 33/33 claim; the corrected units are what section 1 and 4 use.
- We verified the derivation, the wiring and the tool binding at main's own blobs. We did not audit other consumers of `RunnerExecutionCapability` (UI surfaces, remote Runner targets, `/health` consumers), so we make no claim about how the contradiction renders to a human operator.
- The 57 `RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE` / 14 `TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED` payloads are the execution gate behaving as designed; counting them next to the green lights demonstrates a disagreement, not a second defect.
- We take no position on which of the shapes in section 2 is right for the project, and we do not treat the underlying `micromamba` provisioning failure on our host as an SD defect.
1108.title: [Bug]: check_runner reports ready:true for a Runner whose next Shell call is refused with ready:false — the same capability probe, 9 seconds apart

1109.author: JinhZhao
1109.body:
## 1. Actual behaviour

The Native agent loop emits a usage figure after **every** model turn, and each of those figures is written into the run's persisted record stream. The usage ledger receives **one row per run**, and the token fields of that row are the **last main-agent turn only**.

Measured on one captured session (5 runs, 599 per-turn usage records, 5 ledger rows):

| run | ledger rows | main turns with usage | subagent streams | subagent turns with usage | sum of per-turn input tokens, all streams | input tokens in the ledger row | persisted share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `9ceeb1f9` | 1 | 20 | 5 | 572 | 24,023,894 | 44,952 | 0.1871 % |
| `0673152f` | 1 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 300,115 | 47,387 | 15.7896 % |
| `82036958` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |
| `116b288e` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |
| `de7527c9` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | `null` | n/a — no model turn ran |

Session totals: ledger holds 92,339 input / 12,737 output / 6,592 reasoning / 7,168 cache-read tokens; the same session's streams hold 24,324,009 input / 526,865 output / 404,221 reasoning / 13,340,032 cache-read tokens. **0.3796 % of the input the provider reported for the session is in the ledger.**

Four separate things go wrong, and they compound:

1. **A per-run row carries a per-turn number.** In both runs that have tokens, the row equals one specific turn record byte-for-byte and equals no sum: the matching turn is main turn index 19 of 20 for `9ceeb1f9`, main turn index 6 of 7 for `0673152f` — i.e. the last main turn in each case.
2. **Subagent turns contribute nothing.** `9ceeb1f9` ran 5 children over 572 model turns (5,297,320 + 5,055,291 + 5,267,215 + 5,188,821 + 2,398,037 input tokens) and the ledger has 0 rows for them. 96.62 % of that run's per-turn records belong to children. No `invocationKind` exists for them, and the one `subagent.usage` event per child carries that child's *last* turn, never its sum.
3. **The row's time window and its token figures describe different scopes.** `startedAt`/`finishedAt` come from the prompt manifest (the whole run) while the tokens come from one turn: `9ceeb1f9`'s row spans 2 h 50 min 59 s (02:27:15.507Z → 05:18:14.695Z) and reports 56,382 total tokens, whose turn was recorded 0.753 s before the run closed. Any hours-of-run or cost-per-run figure derived from that row is wrong by construction, not by rounding.
4. **The input to the ledger is not reconstructable from the persisted stream.** No stream file in this session contains a single event of type `model_usage` (0 in `9ceeb1f9` main stream with its 20 model turns; 0 in `0673152f` with 7) even though the ledger value is taken from that channel — see `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` in §3, where the handler returns before publishing. An independent audit therefore cannot recompute the row from what is on disk.

What is *not* claimed here: the three rows with all-null token fields are correct as they stand. Those runs contain no `model.completed` record at all (their main streams hold only `run.queued`, `run.started`, `run.status`, `run.cancelled`/`run.failed`), so `usageStatus: "provider-not-reported"` agrees with the recorded stream. This issue is about turns that ran and were not carried into the ledger, not about inventing numbers for runs that made no model call.

## 2. Expected behaviour

1. The ledger reconciles with the provider. For a run of N main turns plus delegated children, the row set for that run must sum to (or be explicitly reconcilable to) the N + ΣM per-turn figures the provider reported and the engine already recorded.
2. Delegated work is attributable. A subagent's model turns are spend of the same run; they need their own `invocationId` and a kind that distinguishes them from the parent's `task`, so a user can answer "what did the delegation cost" — today the answer is only reachable from CAS blobs.
3. A row's figures must describe the row's scope. If one row per invocation is kept as the shape, its tokens have to be the sum over that invocation's turns with the turn count recorded (the engine already returns `turns`), so the duration window and the token window agree.
4. The channel feeding the ledger stays observable. Either the per-turn `model_usage` figures are persisted, or per-turn rows exist — one of the two must hold, so that a reviewer can recompute a stored figure without reading the internal state pool.
5. `provider-not-reported` keeps its current meaning: unknown is recorded as unknown, never as zero. The same discipline this repository already states for the evolve proxy (`evolution/llm-proxy.ts:273-275`).

## 3. Source code

Paths relative to the repository root; all quoted at main `a773942a` / `bec6399d` (identical, §8).

**The engine produces one figure per turn and keeps only the last.**

- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:286` — `let usage: TUsage | undefined;` declared *outside* the turn loop that starts at `:296` (`for (let turn = 0; turn < this.options.maxModelTurns; turn += 1) {`).
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:334-337` — inside the loop, per turn:
  ```
  if (modelTurn.usage !== undefined) {
    usage = modelTurn.usage;
    this.emit({ type: "model_usage", usage });
  }
  ```
  Reassignment, not accumulation; the same pair repeats in the output-recovery retry at `:367-370`.
- `packages/runtime-core/src/runtime.ts:380-384` (normal completion), `:418-419` (suspended return), `:428-432` (turn-budget return) — every exit ships `...(usage !== undefined ? { usage } : {})`, so `AgentLoopResult.usage` is structurally the last turn's usage. `:428-430` shows the result *does* know the count it does not carry: `turns: this.options.maxModelTurns`.

**The agent wrapper forwards that single figure once.**

- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts:647` `let reportedModelUsage = false;`, `:700` `if (event.type === "model_usage") reportedModelUsage = true;`, `:857-858` re-emits each per-turn event upstream (`case "model_usage": emit({ type: "model_usage", usage: event.usage, usageReported: true });`).
- `services/api/src/native-agent/index.ts:715-717`:
  ```
  const usage = result.usage;
  if (!reportedModelUsage) this.emit({ type: "model_usage", ...(usage ? { usage, usageReported: true } : { usageReported: false }) });
  if (usage) this.emit({ type: "usage", usage });
  ```
  The `type: "usage"` event is the terminal, whole-agent figure — one per agent, and (see next) one turn's worth of tokens.

**The run collector holds one overwritten slot, and that slot is what gets persisted.**

- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:1069` `let lastAgentUsage = unreportedModelUsage();` — one variable for the whole run.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2387-2390`:
  ```
  if (event.type === "model_usage") {
    lastAgentUsage = capturedModelUsage(event);
    return;
  }
  ```
  Overwrite per turn, and the early `return` means no `publish(...)` runs for this event type — which is why the persisted stream has 0 `model_usage` records while carrying 20 per-turn usage payloads.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2504` resets the slot to `unreportedModelUsage()` immediately before the run; `:2557` `const taskUsage = lastAgentUsage;`.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2591-2598` (completed), `:2653-2660` (cancelled), `:2700-2707` (failed) — the only three persistence calls on this path, each `invocationKind: "task"`, each passing the same single-slot `usage`. Repo-wide symbol search for `appendModelUsageForManifest` returns three files: its definition, `runs/index.ts` (those call sites), and `services/api/src/http/index.ts:303-306`, which is a re-export list, not a caller. There is no writer in the subagent execution path.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:2109-2114` — the child bridge:
  ```
  if (event.type === "usage") {
    subagent.usage = event.usage;
    finalizeMessageStep();
    void emit({ subagentId: subagent.id, type: "subagent.usage", usage: event.usage });
  ```
  A child's whole-run figure becomes one parent-stream event and one field on the subagent record. It is never handed to `appendModelUsageForManifest`, so children cannot appear in the ledger.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3190-3210` — the other direct writer (`invocationKind: "session-naming"`), also `costUsd: null`.

**The record itself has nowhere to put turn granularity.**

- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:27-35` `CapturedModelUsage` (six token fields + `usageStatus`), `:37-47` `unreportedModelUsage()`, `:49-70` `capturedModelUsage(event)` (returns the event's figures verbatim, or the all-null `provider-not-reported` shape).
- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:72-83` — `appendModelUsageForManifest`'s `options` are `attemptIndex / invocationId / invocationKind / manifest / outcome / runId / usage`: no turn index, no turn count.
- `services/api/src/model-usage/index.ts:85-108` — the record built from them, with `costUsd: null` at `:89`, `finishedAt: options.manifest.finishedAt` at `:90`, `startedAt: options.manifest.createdAt` at `:105`. This is exactly the run-window-plus-one-turn mixture described in §1 item 3.
- `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:167-191` — `ModelInvocationUsage` has `invocationId` (`:175`) and `invocationKind` (`:176`) and no `turnId`, no `turnCount`. `packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:152-162` — `ModelInvocationKind` is `delegation-track | evolve | paper-vision | review-correction | semantic-review | session-naming | task`: no subagent member, and repo-wide literal search for `delegation-track` returns its declaration only, i.e. no writer uses that kind. The manifests are not a workaround either: `runs/index.ts:2587` (and `:2649`, `:2696`) set `turnId: runId`, so the "turn" identifier in the manifest is the run.
- Read side is faithful to its input: `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:57-71` (`addUsageToBucket`) and `:414-448` (`summarizeModelUsageAnalytics`, which sums `usage.inputTokens` per row) and `:385-412` (`estimateInvocationCost`, per row). Nothing here mis-adds — the turns are simply absent from the input. `ModelUsageBucket.invocationCount` (`packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:198`) counts rows, so a 20-turn run and a 1-turn run both count as 1.

**Per-call rows already exist in this codebase.**

- `services/api/src/evolution/llm-proxy.ts:126` `handleEvolveCompletion`, `:162` `const startedAt = new Date().toISOString();`, `:233` `const usage = await recordUsage(deps, grant, model, payload, startedAt);`, `:245-278` `recordUsage(...)` → `parseProviderUsage(payload.usage, …)` then one `appendModelInvocationUsage` per proxied completion, keyed `invocationId: \`evolve:${grant.runId}\`` with its own kind and the comment at `:262-263` justifying a separate kind precisely because "a search's spend is not a chat turn". The same argument applies between a parent's turns and a child's, and between turn 1 and turn 20.

## 4. Real run evidence

One captured session on the integration instance (Native executor, `invocationKind: "task"` rows). Sources: the instance data directory's `model-usage/<sessionId>.json`, `run-events/<sessionId>/<runId>/*.jsonl`, and the per-turn payloads resolved through `versioning/agent-state/blobs/sha256/` (the `payloadRef` of each `model.completed` record). Read-only instruments: `rpH7-persisted-vs-perturN.txt`, `rpH22-e6-usage-census.txt`, `rpH24-e6-usage-events.txt` under `runs/JD/TASK-001/artifacts/`. No credentials or host paths are reproduced below.

Ledger contents for the session (`model-usage/bb1d6797-1270-4bb9-a1a3-a464a5bc141e.json`, 5 rows, all `invocationKind: "task"`, all `costUsd: null`, one row per run):

```
run=9ceeb1f9 outcome=completed usageStatus=reported              in=44952 out=11430 reasoning=6282 cacheRead=3584 total=56382
             startedAt=2026-11-11T02:27:15.507Z finishedAt=2026-11-11T05:18:14.695Z manifest=63d20e49
run=82036958 outcome=cancelled  usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=10:29:00.882Z finishedAt=10:32:45.359Z
run=116b288e outcome=cancelled  usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=10:38:39.403Z finishedAt=10:42:15.250Z
run=de7527c9 outcome=failed     usageStatus=provider-not-reported in=null  out=null  …  startedAt=11:31:22.799Z finishedAt=11:33:44.840Z
run=0673152f outcome=completed  usageStatus=reported              in=47387 out=1307  reasoning=310  cacheRead=3584 total=48694
             startedAt=2026-11-11T11:51:15.241Z finishedAt=2026-11-11T12:03:34.525Z manifest=c2220e9c
```

Per-turn usage recorded in the streams of the same session, by stream:

```
run 9ceeb1f9
  MAIN     turns_with_usage=20   sum(in=817210  out=39005)  first(turn=0  in=24831 out=81   at=02:27:17)  last(turn=19 in=44952 out=11430 at=05:18:13.942)
  sub a426c709 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5297320 out=126948) last(turn=127 in=32017 out=144  at=03:09:44)
  sub c7d68122 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5188821 out=74992)  last(turn=127 in=44707 out=116  at=04:05:29)
  sub c59905d7 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5267215 out=98987)  last(turn=127 in=39699 out=461  at=04:38:24)
  sub b95116e3 turns_with_usage=128  sum(in=5055291 out=100647) last(turn=127 in=43520 out=412  at=05:12:26)
  sub ceb12354 turns_with_usage=60   sum(in=2398037 out=75464)  last(turn=59  in=41592 out=9484 at=03:28:28)
  per-turn usage records: 592 (MAIN=20, subagents=572)   sums: in=24023894 out=516043 reasoning=395528 cacheRead=13174272
  MAIN last turn in=44952 out=11430   persisted row in=44952 out=11430   EQUAL=True
  which per-turn records match the persisted row exactly: [('MAIN', 19)]      row == sum over all streams? False

run 0673152f
  MAIN     turns_with_usage=7    sum(in=300115 out=10822)  first(turn=0 in=31442 out=314 at=11:52:38)  last(turn=6 in=47387 out=1307 at=12:03:32)
  (no subagent streams in this run)
  MAIN last turn in=47387 out=1307   persisted row in=47387 out=1307   EQUAL=True
  which per-turn records match the persisted row exactly: [('MAIN', 6)]       row == sum over all streams? False
```

Which channel the ledger's own numbers arrive on, and what the parent stream holds about children (`main.jsonl` event-type census):

```
run 9ceeb1f9 main.jsonl: {"assistant.thinking.delta":309, "assistant.delta":67, "agent.record":60, "tool.started":43,
                          "tool.completed":43, "plan.updated":26, "record:model.completed":20, "subagent.updated":15,
                          "subagent.usage":5, …}
  events of type model_usage: 0        events carrying a usage dict: 5 (all type=subagent.usage)
    in=32017 out=144  -> matches child a426c709 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=41592 out=9484 -> matches child ceb12354 turn 59  (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=44707 out=116  -> matches child c7d68122 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=39699 out=461  -> matches child c59905d7 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
    in=43520 out=412  -> matches child b95116e3 turn 127 (its last)      matches no MAIN turn record
run 0673152f main.jsonl: {"record:model.completed":7, "agent.record":21, "tool.started":9, …}
  events of type model_usage: 0        events carrying a usage dict: 0
```

So, in one place each: 20 and 7 per-turn figures exist for the parent and 1 survives; 572 per-turn figures exist for the children and 0 reach the ledger while 5 (their last turns) reach the parent stream; and the ledger's surviving figure never appears in the stream as a `model_usage` event, exactly as `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` predicts.

Control for the "are the nulls wrong?" question: the three null-token runs' main streams contain `run.queued: 1, run.started: 1, run.status: 2` plus `run.cancelled: 1` (or `run.failed: 1`) and 0 `model.completed` records — no turn ran, so `provider-not-reported` is accurate and those rows are not counted as losses anywhere in this report.

## 5. Trigger conditions

- **Always, on the Native agent path.** 5 of 5 runs in the captured session produced exactly one row, and 2 of 2 runs that executed model turns produced a row equal to their last main turn. Any run of more than one turn under-reports.
- **Worst exactly where the platform's value is.** A delegated research run lost 572 of 592 turn records (96.62 %) to the missing subagent rows; the more children and the closer they run to the engine's turn ceiling, the larger the blind spot. (`MAX_MODEL_TURNS = 128` at `native-agent/index.ts:102`, applied at `:656` — four of the five children here hit 128.)
- **Not provider-dependent.** The provider reported usage for every turn in these runs; the loss is between the engine and the writer, not at the wire.
- **Not platform-dependent.** No cited line branches on OS; the only Windows-specific code in the chain is unrelated.
- **Silently distorts anything derived from the ledger** — cost estimates (`estimateInvocationCost` per row, `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:385-412`), per-run spend ranking, and the run-duration pairing in §1 item 3 — because the read side trusts the row set.

## 6. Difference from existing Issues and PRs

- **#103** (closed 2026-09-21, `[Feature] Reuse JiuwenSwarm backend - sub-task: Usage`, labels `help wanted`, `priority/major`, `release/0.3.0`) is a *porting* task: bring the JiuwenSwarm backend's usage capability to this repository. It says nothing about how many rows a Native agent run writes or which turn a row describes, and its subject is the swarm gateway path — where, per the symbol search in §3, there is no ledger writer at all. This draft is about the Native executor's writer, whose whole chain (`runtime-core` → `native-agent` → `runs/index.ts` → `model-usage/index.ts`) post-dates #103's scope. **Not the same request.**
- **#304** (open PR, `fix: parse usage by protocol and keep real E2E accounting non-gating`, created 2026-10-14) changes `.ci/README.md` plus three test files (`packages/model/src/client.test.ts`, `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts`, `test/journey-basic-real-api.spec.ts`) and touches no production writer. Its stated principle — missing accounting is diagnostic evidence, not evidence of zero cost — is the same principle §2 item 5 asks this Issue to preserve, and its body explicitly notes that the protocol-aware parser already lives on main in `packages/model/src/usage.ts` (`normalizeUsage`). It resolves *how a reported figure is parsed*, never *how many figures are stored*. **Adjacent, not duplicate.**
- **#783 / #789** (closed) and **#811** (closed PR `fix(model): preserve reasoning token diagnostics`) are arithmetic/diagnostic correctness on a figure that is already in the row: cached-prompt double-charging (fixed at `services/api/src/model-usage.ts:392-398`) and reasoning-token preservation. They assume the row's token fields are the run's true counts. That assumption is what this report measures and finds false for multi-turn and delegated runs.
- **#858 / #861 / #873 / #882 / #912** (closed) and **#509 / #575** (open) concern the usage page's headers, date presets, formatting and entry points — display-layer scoping of the stored rows. Nothing proposes or performs a change to `appendModelUsageForManifest`.
- **#330** (closed, session timeline showing tokens) and **#854 / #550** (closed, subagent panel) consume the per-child `subagent.usage` figure; they establish that the child's *last-turn* number is already user-visible while the ledger holds nothing at all about children. That is the display/record asymmetry §2 item 2 asks to close, not a prior report of it.
- **#963** (closed PR, record judge tokens, session tokens and tool calls on the real-case table) writes a CI artifact in the benchmark pipeline, not `ModelInvocationUsage`.
- Searches run against the live repository index: `usage granularity` → 2 records, neither relevant; `ModelInvocationUsage` → #783, #811; `usage ledger` → #304, #963, #330, #789 among others, none about persistence granularity; `subagent usage` → no record stating that a child's model turns are absent from the usage ledger. No record proposes per-turn or per-model-call rows for the Native agent path.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

1. **Reconciliation.** For a Native run of N main turns, the stored rows for that `runId` sum to the provider-reported per-turn figures the engine emitted for it (or the difference is an explicit, named state, e.g. `turnsRecorded` vs `turnsTotal`). A test with N ≥ 3 asserts the sum, not the last value.
2. **Children are in the ledger.** A run that delegates to K subagents stores their turn spend with its own `invocationId` and a kind distinguishable from the parent's `task` — either a new `ModelInvocationKind` member or a writer for the already-declared but unused `delegation-track` (`packages/schema/src/model-usage.ts:152-162`) — plus the parent linkage that today exists only as `subagentId` on the stream event.
3. **Scope agreement.** Whichever shape is chosen, a row's token fields describe the same scope as its `startedAt`/`finishedAt`. If one row per run is retained, its tokens are the run's sums and the row carries the turn count the engine already returns (`runtime.ts:418`, `:430`).
4. **Recomputable from persisted evidence.** Either `model_usage` figures reach the run's stream (remove the pre-publish `return` at `runs/index.ts:2387-2390` or publish a distinct record) or per-turn rows exist — one of the two, so a reviewer can recompute any stored figure from the record directory alone.
5. **Unknown stays unknown.** A run with zero completed model turns keeps `usageStatus: "provider-not-reported"` with null fields, per §4's control and #304's stated policy; the fix must not materialise zeros.
6. **Derived figures follow.** With rows corrected, `summarizeModelUsageAnalytics` and `estimateInvocationCost` need no change; add a test that a 20-turn delegated run's estimated cost is roughly 20×-plus-children that of a 1-turn run, so a regression to last-turn-only persistence fails loudly.
7. **Docstring parity.** The `ModelInvocationUsage` comment space or the usage page documents what a row means after the change, since "invocation" today silently denotes "run" on one path and "call" on the evolve path.

## Limitations of this report

- Run evidence is one session (5 runs, 2 of them multi-turn) on a Windows host. The 1-of-N collapse and the missing `model_usage` events were reproduced in both multi-turn runs and follow directly from code with no platform branch, but we have not measured the same shape on Linux or with the JiuwenSwarm executor.
- Per-turn figures were recovered from the `payloadRef` of each persisted `model.completed` record (the agent-state CAS). We verified that the ledger row equals one of those records; we did not verify them against provider invoices, so "what the provider reported" here means "what the provider reported per turn into this pipeline".
- The instance executes the build product of the fork at `30178fda7…`. We proved the *source* blobs for every cited file match main; we did not byte-verify the compiled `dist/` of this cited module against that source.
- `costUsd` is null in every row this writer produces (`model-usage/index.ts:89`, and `runs/index.ts:3194` for the naming path). Cost is an estimate made at read time from pricing tables; the §5 claim that cost inherits the undercount is derived from that code path, not from a usage-page measurement — we did not exercise the analytics UI.
